title: A Clock for the Harbor
premise: In 1898, in the fog-bound harbor city of Port Calloway, Juniper Vasquez — daughter of a drowned pearl diver and indentured to the Meridian Trading Company — has learned that history is something that happens to other people, elsewhere. But when a sealed letter surfaces naming her family as silent partners in the company's founding fraud, Juniper discovers that her mother's death, her father's debts, and the harbor's very map were built on a buried crime. Racing the company's fixers and its hired historian across one desperate week, she gathers testimony from divers, dockworkers, and a dying clerk who kept the ledger. At dawn on the sailing tide, she must get the truth notarized and into the hands of a federal investigator before the ship — carrying the evidence's only other copy — leaves for good; she succeeds at the cost of her indenture contract, burned before her eyes, and walks free into a city that finally knows her name.
about_author: Sebastian Galloway is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipping ledgers along the Pacific coast. Their novels excavate the small betrayals hidden inside great commercial fortunes.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Juniper Vasquez, seventeen and indentured to Meridian Trading since her pearl diver father drowned, dives the harbor pilings at dawn to clear fouled chains. POV: Juniper. She catalogs the harbor's rhythms like scripture, convinced history belongs to capitals and wars, never to people like her. Emotional beat: quiet resignation mistaken for contentment.

chapters.title: A Letter Sealed Twice
chapters.summary: A dying company clerk, Elias Thorn, presses a sealed letter into Juniper's hands at the countinghouse door, whispering that it names 'the Vasquez line' in something old and rotten. POV: Juniper. Her supervisor intercepts her questions with practiced warmth. Emotional beat: the first crack — curiosity curdling into unease as she realizes someone is watching her.

chapters.title: What Mother Kept Under the Floor
chapters.summary: Juniper pries up her late mother's floorboards and finds a diver's slate covered in numbers matching the letter's references. POV: Juniper, with a flashback to her mother teaching her slate-writing underwater. Emotional beat: grief re-opened; the dead begin speaking, and Juniper can no longer pretend her family stood outside of history.

chapters.title: The Company's Kind Historian
chapters.summary: Meridian's house historian, Mr. Aldous Crane, visits Juniper with gifts and gentle warnings about 'slander against benefactors.' POV: alternating Juniper and Crane, whose polished chapters reveal his talent for making crimes into legends. Emotional beat: charm as threat; Juniper understands the past is being actively managed, and she is standing on the page being rewritten.

chapters.title: Divers' Tongues
chapters.summary: Juniper seeks out Old Maren, a retired diver who once worked her father's crew, and learns the founding fleet carried contraband under pearl cargo — and that witnesses are fewer every year. POV: Maren's voice dominates through told memory. Emotional beat: solidarity across generations; Juniper stops asking whether to act and starts asking how.

chapters.title: Indenture Is a Long Word for Chain
chapters.summary: Crane escalates: Juniper's contract is suddenly 'under review,' threatening her with debtors' island if she talks. POV: Juniper, interrogated in a lamplit office. Emotional beat: fear and fury braided together; loyalty to the company that fed her collides headlong with the truth about what that feeding cost.

chapters.title: The Clerk Who Counted Everything
chapters.summary: Juniper finds Thorn alive but failing in a charity ward; he confesses he copied the original ledger before Crane's predecessor burned it, and hid half in the customs house. POV: Thorn's deathbed narration interwoven with Juniper's. Emotional beat: a coward's redemption; Thorn asks forgiveness, and Juniper must decide if truth delivered too late still counts.

chapters.title: Tide Tables and Timetables
chapters.summary: Juniper maps the week ahead: the mail steamer Persephone sails on the morning tide in six days, carrying Crane and the company's official archive to London. POV: Juniper, planning with dockworker ally Sam Okonkwo. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into strategy; the race now has a finish line drawn in water.

chapters.title: Customs House, After Hours
chapters.summary: A night infiltration of the customs house yields half the ledger — pages proving the founding fraud — but a watchman is bribed by Crane's men, and Juniper barely escapes unseen. POV: Juniper, tense second-person-adjacent interiority. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by paranoia; every friendly face becomes suspect.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed My Father's Death
chapters.summary: Juniper confronts harbormaster DeWitt, whose falsified dive logs sent her father down unsafely to silence him decades ago. POV: DeWitt's guilt-ridden confession, then Juniper's cold clarity. Emotional beat: rage without satisfaction; vengeance proves hollow next to the record she needs to build.

chapters.title: Sam's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sam Okonkwo reveals he was paid to report on Juniper — then tears up the money and offers his network of longshoremen instead. POV: Sam. Emotional beat: betrayal confessed and forgiven; loyalty is chosen, not owed, and Juniper learns trust is a risk worth taking twice.

chapters.title: Crane Writes a Counterfeit Night
chapters.summary: Crane publishes a serialized 'true history' of Meridian in the Gazette, recasting the fraud as heroic sacrifice and painting the Thorn letter as forgery. POV: Crane, savoring his craft. Emotional beat: dread; Juniper watches the victors' history print itself in real time and understands the deadline is also a narrative war.

chapters.title: The Divers Strike the Chains
chapters.summary: Harbor divers refuse to service Meridian's ships until the ledger is read publicly; the strike gives Juniper cover but paints a target on the community. POV: ensemble, anchored by Maren. Emotional beat: collective courage; Juniper sees her private quest become a public cause and feels its weight.

chapters.title: What the Slate Couldn't Hold
chapters.summary: Decoding her mother's slate fully, Juniper learns her mother witnessed the fraud's cover-up and chose silence to protect the family — the letter's 'guilt' is real. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: devastating ambiguity; her mother was both victim and accomplice, forcing Juniper to hold love and judgment in one hand.

chapters.title: Island of Debtors
chapters.summary: Crane has Thorn's ward records seized and Juniper summoned to the debtors' island; Sam smuggles her off before the ferry docks. POV: Juniper, hunted through mudflats at night. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into commitment; there is no version of her life now where she goes back to diving pilings quietly.

chapters.title: The Notary Who Owes No One
chapters.summary: Juniper finds the one notary in Port Calloway untouchable by Meridian — a disgraced judge, Odile Ferrant — who agrees to certify testimonies if Juniper brings every living witness in person. POV: Ferrant's wry perspective. Emotional beat: cautious hope; the machinery of truth exists, but it demands everything Juniper has left.

chapters.title: Testimony by Lamplight
chapters.summary: One long night of depositions: Maren, Sam, the watchman, DeWitt, and Thorn's copied pages, sworn and sealed while Crane's men circle the block. POV: rotating witness voices framed by Juniper. Emotional beat: solemn triumph; the record exists now — but paper means nothing until it reaches the right hands.

chapters.title: The Bribe
chapters.summary: Crane offers Juniper freedom, passage to London, and her family name cleared in exchange for the originals; he shows her a forged confession implicating her mother as sole architect. POV: Juniper and Crane, face to face. Emotional beat: the darkest hour; the offer is genuinely tempting, and protecting her mother's memory argues for silence.

chapters.title: Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Dawn. The Persephone loads; Crane boards with the official archive. Juniper, witnesses behind her, must get the certified dossier to federal investigator Reyes at the pier before the gangway lifts. POV: Juniper, minute by minute. Emotional beat: white-knuckle climax; the whole book converges on one stretch of wet planking.

chapters.title: Served at the Gangway
chapters.summary: Blocked by Crane's men, Juniper invokes an archaic harbor right — any diver may serve papers on a vessel in port — and swims the last hundred yards to hand Reyes the dossier as the lines are cast off. POV: Juniper, underwater, echoing her parents' trade. Emotional beat: catharsis; the skill that bound her becomes the instrument of her liberation.

chapters.title: The Historian Unwritten
chapters.summary: Reyes impounds the ship's archive; Crane, exposed, chooses to sail into disgrace rather than face the harbor he defamed. Juniper's indenture is voided, the contract burned on the customs house steps. POV: Crane's bitter epilogue-voice, then Juniper watching the fire. Emotional beat: justice without gloating; the victors' historian becomes a footnote.

chapters.title: A Clock for the Harbor
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the harbor clock — stopped since the fraud, per legend — is repaired and rings again as Juniper, now employed cataloguing the recovered ledger for the public record, teaches children to write on slates like her mother taught her. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: earned peace; history happened to her after all, and now she keeps it for everyone else.
